clue.text: Sailors who have many relations?

definitions.meaning: an informal British word for seamen
split into two words, people who pair up with plenty of partners ...

explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as two words: those who MATE LOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang, from French, for a sailor or naval rating.

clue.text: The legend of Arachne? That's a tall story!

definitions.meaning: split legend into leg-end: the end of a leg of the setter Arachne, a spider, speaking of herself

explanation.walkthrough: Arachne is the setter, named for the spider of myth; a leg-end, the end of her leg, is her foot, and she says 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses scornful disbelief at a claim, just as one greets an obvious tall story.

clue.text: Rang and gave away secrets on air

indicators.note: broadcast speech is heard rather than read, so the words before are taken by their sound

parts.note: someone who told has blabbed or given away a secret

explanation.surface: A broadcaster phoned in and leaked confidential information live.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells that rang have sounded out with slow strokes, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Charms spoil with time, so get on with it!

parts.note: good looks are a person's attractive features or charms
to mar is to spoil or damage

explanation.surface: Good looks fade over the years, so hurry up and make the most of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an imperative urging someone to hurry up, the same as the clue's exhortation.

clue.text: What you will otherwise do on 6 January

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's comedy is subtitled 'Or What You Will', so otherwise means alternatively titled
a do is a party; the evening of the Epiphany festivities falls around 5 or 6 January

explanation.walkthrough: 'Otherwise' means 'also known as': the play's full title is Twelfth Night, or What You Will. 'Do' is a British word for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play carries the alternative title What You Will, and the Epiphany celebration bears the same name.

clue.text: Fully committed, dad and I join Unionists

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A father declares he is wholeheartedly signing up with the Unionists.
explanation.definitionFit: A paid-up member has paid all dues and so is a wholehearted, committed supporter.

clue.text: A sector of Fukushima was hazardously thus

indicators.note: sector says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the Japanese nuclear site was dangerously flooded after the tsunami.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the scene; 'thus' points back at it, standing for the state the hidden run describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fukushima was flooded by the tsunami, so the plant was in that drenched condition the clue refers to.

clue.text: Feyerabend finally is in favour of falsification

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the philosopher's surname

parts.note: taken as written
pro means in favour of
taken as written

explanation.surface: The philosopher of science Paul Feyerabend ultimately backs Popper's falsification principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsification is the act of showing a claim to be false, which is a refutation or proof against it.

clue.text: Postured preposterously, having highest opinion of oneself

indicators.note: something done preposterously is absurdly out of order, so the letters of the previous word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone posed absurdly, being the most conceited person present.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean conceited or arrogant, and this superlative names the most self-regarding.

clue.text: Acolyte starts to forswear open-mindedness, like one of the herd?

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: a cow lows, so a member of the herd is something that lows

explanation.surface: A disciple gives up independent thinking and becomes a sheep in the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like part of the surface comparison but is the third word whose first letter is taken. LOWER here is one who moos, not 'below'.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an attendant or devoted adherent, a disciple who trails behind a leader.

clue.text: Spooner's to kill writer and collect £200!

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two pieces trade places

parts.note: to gas is to kill with poison gas
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: A Monopoly player is told to do away with an author and pick up the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: In the board game Monopoly a player who goes past the GO square is paid £200 (in the US, $200).
explanation.definitionFit: The board-game instruction pairs moving beyond the starting square with banking the salary, so the clue quotes its other half.

clue.text: Finish like Marie Curie?

definitions.meaning: a glossy shellac surface applied to wood furniture
the scientist was born in Poland and became a French citizen, so both nationalities

explanation.walkthrough: Marie Curie was Polish by birth and French by marriage and naturalisation; 'Polish' loses its capital in the wood finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellac technique gives wooden furniture a high-gloss surface coat, a type of final treatment.

clue.text: Couple in USA regularly picked flowers

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the phrase, starting with the second, is a regular selection

explanation.surface: A pair of Americans gathered blooms on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' looks like a noun but is the verb: a bud flowers, that is, opens.
explanation.definitionFit: When a blossom flowers it unfolds its petals, the same as a bud doing this.

clue.text: Helped hide the claret?

parts.note: fur is an animal's hide or pelt
taken as written
claret is a red wine, and also a dark red colour

explanation.surface: Someone assisted in concealing the bottle of Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb but is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To further a cause is to advance or promote it, so assisted it along.

clue.text: Plots involving high-speed races

parts.note: Mach I, Mach one, is the speed of sound
a race can mean a people or nation

explanation.surface: Schemes that include fast motor racing events.
explanation.walkthrough: MACH I is read as Mach one, the roman numeral giving the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Machinations are crafty schemes or intrigues, the same as secret conspiracies.

clue.text: Farsi can become français, if you do this

definitions.text: Farsi can become français, if you do this

parts.words: Farsi can become français, if you do this
parts.note: rendering the Persian language into French is turning one tongue into another, though the letters of Farsi can tempt a solver to rearrange them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Farsi can' looks like anagram fodder for 'français', but the clue simply describes rendering one language into another.
explanation.definitionFit: To render text from Persian into French is to convert it between languages, the act described.

clue.text: Away I step, ill-prepared — or not prepared — for skiing

parts.note: off means away, as in 'be off'

indicators.note: badly made ready, so the letters of the two words before are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A skier leaves unprepared, or onto snow that has not been groomed.
explanation.walkthrough: On the slopes, a piste is a ski run that has been groomed and prepared, so 'ill-prepared' doubles as a sly hint at the snow itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing outside groomed runs is skiing on snow that has not been made ready for skiers.

clue.text: Browning perhaps subverting cosy oral tale

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something upside down reads it from the bottom up

parts.note: snug means cosy

indicators.note: an oral account is spoken, so the next word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a myth is a traditional tale

explanation.surface: The poet Robert Browning is perhaps undermining a comfortable spoken story.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning suggests the poet but means John Browning, the American firearms designer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Moses Browning designed and made firearms, so he is an example of a weapons maker.

clue.text: Source of retired aunt's tailored, fashionable top

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the short word is read backwards
cut and altered like a suit, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
in means fashionable
the head is the top of something

explanation.surface: An aunt who has retired wears a tailored, stylish blouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountainhead is the spring at which a stream rises, hence any origin.

clue.text: I have supper after ten

indicators.note: after places the eating word behind the number

parts.note: 10 written as the letters I and O
to dine is to eat an evening meal

explanation.surface: Someone eats their evening meal once ten o'clock has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single letter I, the chemical symbol for this element.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the chemical symbol of the halogen element with atomic number 53.

clue.text: Showing no emotion as muscle gets caught in zip

indicators.note: something caught in a garment is trapped inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the fly is the zip on a pair of trousers
lat is short for latissimus dorsi, a back muscle

explanation.surface: Someone stays deadpan when their flesh is snagged in a zipper.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking flatly means speaking in a monotone, without expression or feeling.

clue.text: Haiti cops dressed in pale green

indicators.note: dressing arranges or prepares something, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Police officers in Haiti are wearing light green uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistachio names the pale yellowish-green colour of the nut's kernel.

clue.text: Principle aside, love to get married!

parts.note: read as 'a side', a team of eleven players, written XI in Roman numerals
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Putting one's principles to one side, someone falls for a partner and weds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aside' splits as A SIDE: a cricket or football team has eleven players, so a side is XI.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth or established rule, a fundamental principle.

clue.text: Corrupt president's interment

annotationWithheld.why: Corrupt president's interment (5): SPOIL is P inside SOIL, but 'interment' has to supply both SOIL and the container indicator, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: Energy supply? Dave ignored privatised wrongdoing

indicators.note: doing something wrongly scrambles it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Dave Cameron's letters are removed from the fodder, the remainder being the answer

explanation.surface: Prime Minister David Cameron overlooked misconduct in the privatised power industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignored' tells you DAVE's letters are taken out of PRIVATISED; 'wrongdoing' rearranges what is left, PRITIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit, as in motor spirit or methylated spirit, is a fuel, so it supplies energy.

clue.text: She's over-groomed

parts.note: she has more grooms than allowed, that is more than one husband

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over-groomed' suggests too much preening, but a groom here is a bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with two husbands at once has married unlawfully twice, the offence named.

clue.text: Unearth old philosopher

parts.note: ex means former or old
David Hume, the Scottish Enlightenment philosopher

explanation.surface: Dig up the remains of an ancient thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig a buried body out of the ground, literally to bring it out of the earth.

clue.text: Stealing 80% of everything movable

indicators.note: letters that can be moved are rearranged
the word has ten letters, so eighty percent is its first eight

explanation.surface: A burglar takes most of the portable possessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 80% of EVERYTHING is EVERYTHI, which 'movable' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Thievery is the practice of theft, a synonym for taking what belongs to others.
